blueprint_topic: Mechanism of action and safe medication knowledge for inhaled anticholinergic therapy
stem: A nurse is reviewing the mechanism of action of ipratropium bromide (ATROVENT HFA), prescribed for maintenance treatment of bronchospasm associated with COPD. Which action best explains its bronchodilator effect?

options.A: Stimulation of beta2-adrenergic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle
options.B: Antagonism of acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle
options.C: Blockade of leukotriene receptors in the airways
options.D: Activation of intracellular glucocorticoid receptors to suppress airway inflammation

rationale: B is correct. ATROVENT HFA is an anticholinergic (parasympatholytic) medication. Its current prescribing information states that ipratropium antagonizes the action of acetylcholine and prevents the intracellular calcium increase produced by acetylcholine interaction with muscarinic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle. A describes the mechanism of beta2-adrenergic agonists, not ipratropium. C describes leukotriene-receptor antagonism. D describes the receptor mechanism of corticosteroids. The final item therefore tests the specific labeled mechanism without the vague or obviously false alternatives present in the source item.
educational_objective: Recognize that inhaled ipratropium produces bronchodilation through anticholinergic antagonism of acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
source_document_title: ATROVENT HFA (ipratropium bromide HFA inhalation aerosol)
source_version_date: DailyMed page updated 2025-11-05; prescribing information revised 2024-12; current label accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: DailyMed Set ID 170e98ef-5560-4068-be7d-e649068eb884. Section 1 'Indications and Usage': ATROVENT HFA is an anticholinergic bronchodilator for maintenance treatment of bronchospasm associated with COPD. Section 12.1 'Mechanism of Action': ipratropium is an anticholinergic/parasympatholytic agent that antagonizes acetylcholine and prevents the intracellular calcium increase caused by acetylcholine interaction with muscarinic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle.
source_claim_supported: The current official label directly supports ipratropium's anticholinergic mechanism through antagonism of acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle and its maintenance bronchodilator use in COPD.

correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The generic FDA landing page was replaced with a current ATROVENT HFA label and exact Section 12.1 locator. The distractors were rebuilt as competing, real pharmacologic mechanisms rather than vague or self-disqualifying statements.
audit_findings: The source's generic label URL did not establish an exact mechanism locator.
Current ATROVENT HFA labeling directly describes the anticholinergic mechanism in Section 12.1.
The source distractors included vague or obviously impossible statements; they were replaced by real competing drug-class mechanisms.
The indication context was preserved as COPD maintenance therapy without adding unsupported claims about rescue use.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct mechanism, no second answer, no cueing, no unsupported numerical precision, and appropriate NCLEX pharmacology alignment.
